ENT TELEHEALTH NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Sudden onset shortness of breath at rest while watching TV; no specific trigger identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Dyspnea began ~1 hour ago, described as “a bit short of breath.” Yesterday developed a dry, non-productive cough. Palpitations noted during current episode. No prior similar episodes.
- ENT symptoms: Denies throat tightness/closure, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling, ear pain/hearing changes, or neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: None; no previous hospitalizations for respiratory issues.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergy: Ibuprofen – reaction not specified.  
  • Medications: Codeine (post-operative analgesia); last dose ≈1 week ago; dose/route/frequency not documented. No other meds reported.
- Social context: 43-year-old woman (DOB stated 20 Apr 1980; clinician repeated 1983—see Quality checks) at home alone with 4-week-old baby; partner at work.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None reported or seen.
- Airway/breathing: Patient conversational; no reported stridor or wheeze. Self-counted radial pulse 30 beats over an assumed 15 s interval (~120 bpm) → tachycardia.
- Mental status/associated features: Alert; reports feeling “stressed.” No dizziness or syncope reported.
- Vitals/exam: Not recorded (no RR, BP, SpO₂, temperature, or detailed chest exam).
- Accompaniment: Baby present; no other adult in home.

Assessment:
- Working impression: Suspected pulmonary embolism (post-partum) causing acute dyspnea and tachycardia.
  Evidence: 4 weeks post-cesarean (hypercoagulable state), sudden onset dyspnea at rest, pleuritic chest soreness on deep inspiration, tachycardia, family history of clots (mother), no preceding exertion.
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with DDx):
  1. Pulmonary embolism – high likelihood; multiple risk factors and classic presentation.
  2. Acute lower-respiratory infection (viral/bacterial) – moderate likelihood; presence of new cough, but onset of breathlessness sudden and no fever; opposing evidence: no sputum, afebrile, higher VTE risk.
  3. Anxiety/panic episode – moderate likelihood; patient feels stressed with palpitations; opposing evidence: objective risk factors and pleuritic discomfort.
- No transcript evidence for angioedema, anaphylaxis, airway obstruction, or other primary ENT pathologies.

Plan:
- Immediate action: Patient advised to proceed promptly to nearest hospital Emergency Department for further evaluation of possible pulmonary embolism (imaging ± labs). Ambulance offered; patient prefers self-transport with infant.
- Medications: Advised to withhold codeine until evaluated.
- Instructions & red flags:
  • Seek emergency help (999/EMS) immediately if worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, throat tightness, syncope, or inability to breathe/speak in full sentences.  
  • Remain accompanied once possible; bring baby supplies to hospital.
- Follow-up: ED assessment today; anticipate need for imaging (CT pulmonary angiography or V/Q scan) and blood work (d-dimer, CBC, coagulation). Consider postpartum VTE prophylaxis and possible anticoagulation if PE confirmed. Referral to obstetrics and hematology as indicated.
- Education: Explained rationale for evaluation; patient verbalized understanding and agreement.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Full vital signs (RR, BP, SpO₂, temperature); detailed chest/ENT exam; description of ibuprofen allergy reaction; smoking status; anticoagulation prophylaxis history; availability of childcare/escort; clarification of pulse count interval.  
● Transcript/DDx conflicts: DOB—patient states 20 Apr 1980; clinician restates 1983 (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; no inaudible sections.
